title: Mozilla launches Firefox Enterprise to give European firms more choice — new browser gives government, healthcare and finance more control over how they use the web, handle sensitive data and access AI tools
key_facts: Mozilla introduced Firefox Enterprise, a version of its browser for organizations that need extra security, governance and compliance controls (TechRadar).
Customers can choose where data is stored and how it is governed, and it is designed to work with existing identity, security-monitoring and device-management systems.

Mozilla argues that businesses depend on a small number of tech companies; it says other browsers lean largely on Google's Chromium and Apple's WebKit, while Firefox runs on Mozilla's own Gecko engine.
Mozilla CEO Anthony Enzor-DeMeo is quoted: "If all your options are built with the same technology underneath, 'choice' is a lie."
Firefox claims 200 million monthly users but, per Statcounter, has 6% of desktop browsing sessions against 65% for Chrome.
France, Germany, Austria and Switzerland get Firefox Enterprise first, with other countries later; Thunderbird Enterprise (email) is in development.
quote_evidence: Mozilla has introduced Firefox Enterprise, a brand-new version of its browser designed specifically for organizations that need extra security, governance and compliance controls.
France, Germany, Austria and Switzerland will be the first countries to get access to Firefox Enterprise, with other countries added later on.
Firefox claims to have 200 million monthly users, but per Statcounter data, it only accounts for 6% of desktop browsing sessions globally compared with 65% for Chrome.
why_it_matters_hint: A browser for organizations, with control over where data sits, is offered as an alternative to Chrome-based and Safari-based browsers in Europe.
notes: Full text read. TechRadar's headline says the browser gives control over how firms "access AI tools", but the article text says nothing about AI, so the AI link is not established; score lowered 5 to 4 for that reason. No price or availability date beyond the four launch countries.
